input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run parameters and metrics retrieval for multi-run comparison (Data Science Pipelines backend)

## Description

This epic delivers the Data Science Pipelines backend support that makes run
parameters and metrics retrievable for a selected set of runs, in a form the
Dashboard can consume to render multi-run comparisons. Today run parameters and
metrics are only accessible through per-run pages; comparing runs requires
exporting to spreadsheets. This epic provides the run-data foundation for the
platform's experiment comparison capability.

## Scope

- Extend the Data Science Pipelines run-data surfaces so that parameters and
  metrics for a user-selected set of runs can be retrieved together, covering
  the run kinds surfaced in the platform's runs list (training and pipeline
  runs).
- Keep retrieval consistent with the existing per-run parameter and metric data
  already shown in run detail pages — no changes to how parameters and metrics
  are recorded, only how they can be retrieved for comparison.
- Preserve backward compatibility: existing per-run retrieval behavior and the
  DataSciencePipelinesApplication deployment model are unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a set of two or more runs selected in the platform, their parameters
  and metrics can be retrieved together through the Data Science Pipelines
  run-data surface in a single logical operation suitable for side-by-side
  rendering.
- The retrieval returns consistent parameter and metric data for runs that
  declare different sets of parameters and metrics (missing values are
  representable, not errors).
- Existing per-run retrieval and run detail behavior is unchanged (no
  regression to current run pages).
- The capability is available for the run kinds the Dashboard's runs list
  surfaces today.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and
  metrics side by side in the Dashboard — this epic provides the backend
  run-data retrieval that the Dashboard comparison view renders.

# Run selection, side-by-side comparison and diff view in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers the experiment comparison user experience in the Dashboard:
users select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by
side, with changed values highlighted when comparing two runs. This replaces
the exported-spreadsheet workflow data scientists use today to compare training
and pipeline runs, giving model promotion decisions side-by-side visibility
into what changed between candidate runs. The view renders run parameters and
metrics retrieved through the Data Science Pipelines run-data retrieval
capability delivered elsewhere in this strategy.

## Scope

- Add run selection from the Dashboard runs list: users can select two or more
  runs and open a comparison view.
- Render selected runs' parameters and metrics side by side, aligned by
  parameter/metric name.
- When exactly two runs are compared, highlight which parameters and metrics
  changed between them (values that differ, added, or missing on either side).
- Handle runs that declare different sets of parameters and metrics gracefully
  (missing values shown as such, not as errors).
- Keep comparison within a single project (no cross-cluster or cross-project
  comparison, per the strategy's out-of-scope list); no automatic best-run
  selection or promotion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a runs list, when a user selects two or more runs and opens the
  comparison, then the selected runs' parameters and metrics are displayed side
  by side, aligned by name.
- Given exactly two selected runs, when the comparison is displayed, then
  parameters and metrics whose values changed between the two runs are
  highlighted.
- Given selected runs with differing parameter/metric sets, when the comparison
  is displayed, then values missing from a run are represented as missing
  rather than causing an error.
- The comparison is available from within a single project only; automatic
  best-run selection and promotion are not part of this capability.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and
  metrics side by side in the Dashboard.
- HLR-3 (P1) (bundled with HLR-1): The run "diff" view highlighting which
  parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs is a presentation
  mode of the same comparison surface over the same run data as HLR-1 — one
  capability consolidated from two customer councils, delivered by this single
  epic at the higher priority. Splitting it would build the same surface twice
  and add an artificial serialization edge.

# Run lineage link on registered model versions

## Description

This epic delivers the Model Registry capability that links a registered model
version back to the run that produced it. Registered model versions become
traceable to their originating training or pipeline run, so a comparison can be
opened from the Model Registry. The Model Registry's custom properties on model
versions are the extension point for attaching this structured metadata.

## Scope

- Enable a registered model version to carry a reference to the run that
  produced it, using the model-version extension point (custom properties).
- Make the run reference retrievable through the existing OpenAPI-specified
  Model Registry REST API surface, extending it only as needed for this
  metadata.
- Preserve backward compatibility: existing RegisteredModel / ModelVersion /
  ModelArtifact entities, custom properties, and API behavior are unaffected
  for model versions that carry no run reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version produced by a run, when the run reference is
  recorded, then the model version persistently carries a retrievable
  reference identifying the producing run.
- The run reference is retrievable through the Model Registry REST API for
  consuming UIs.
- Model versions without a run reference continue to be created, read, and
  managed exactly as before (no regression to existing registry behavior).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): Registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry — this epic
  persists and exposes the link; the registry-side user entry point is
  delivered by the Dashboard registry integration in this strategy.

# Open a run comparison from the Model Registry UI

## Description

This epic delivers the Model Registry user entry point for experiment
comparison: from a registered model version in the registry UI, a user can open
a comparison of the run that produced it against other runs. It surfaces the
run reference persisted on registered model versions and launches the
platform's run comparison capability seeded with that run, so model promotion
decisions can start from the registry rather than only from the runs list.

## Scope

- In the Dashboard's Model Registry UI, surface the run reference carried by a
  registered model version (delivered by the Model Registry run-lineage work in
  this strategy).
- Provide an action from a model version that opens the run comparison
  capability (delivered by the Dashboard comparison work in this strategy)
  seeded with the producing run.
- Degrade gracefully for model versions that carry no run reference (no action
  or a disabled state, not an error).
- Keep the flow within a single project (no cross-cluster or cross-project
  comparison, per the strategy's out-of-scope list).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that carries a run reference, when a user
  triggers the compare action in the registry UI, then the run comparison view
  opens seeded with the producing run so further runs can be selected for
  side-by-side comparison.
- Given a registered model version without a run reference, when its detail is
  viewed, then the UI degrades gracefully with no errors.
- The registry entry point and the runs-list entry point lead to the same
  comparison capability (no duplicate comparison surface is built).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): Registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry — this epic
  delivers the registry-side user entry point that consumes the persisted run
  reference.

# Document the experiment comparison workflow

## Description

This epic documents the experiment comparison capability for training and
pipeline runs once it is implemented: how users select runs and compare
parameters and metrics side by side, how changed values are highlighted between
two runs, and how to open a comparison from a registered model version in the
Model Registry.

## Scope

Content outline (within the Red Hat docs content process):

- Comparison from the runs list: selecting two or more runs, reading the
  side-by-side parameters and metrics view, and interpreting the highlighted
  changes between two runs.
- Comparison from the Model Registry: opening a comparison from a registered
  model version that links back to its producing run, and the behavior for
  versions without a run reference.
- Scope boundaries users should know: comparison is within a single project;
  there is no automatic best-run selection or promotion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers the comparison workflow from both entry
  points: the runs list and the Model Registry.
- The documentation describes the diff highlighting between two selected runs
  and the single-project scope boundary.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented comparison
  capability before publication (reviewed by or with the implementing teams).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs
  list and the registry.
